name: Amwell Converge vs Teladoc Health
title: Amwell Converge vs Teladoc Health: Enterprise Telehealth Platforms
description: Compare Amwell Converge (enterprise hybrid care, KLAS 80.1) vs Teladoc Health (90M+ members, public company). Enterprise telehealth infrastructure solutions.

summary.bottom_line: Amwell Converge and Teladoc Health serve different enterprise needs. Amwell Converge is infrastructure for health systems to build hybrid care programs - integrating virtual and in-person care with EHR, RPM devices, and clinical workflows. Teladoc Health provides turnkey telehealth services with its own physician network. Amwell = platform for health systems to use their own providers. Teladoc = complete virtual care service.

key_differences.providers: Amwell: Health system's own | Teladoc: Teladoc network
key_differences.integration: Amwell: Deep EHR/RPM | Teladoc: Standard integrations

sections.heading: Platform vs Service
sections.content: Amwell Converge and Teladoc serve fundamentally different needs. Amwell Converge is infrastructure - a platform health systems use to deliver virtual care with their own providers, integrated into their EHR and clinical workflows. Teladoc is a complete service - it provides the technology, the physicians, and manages the entire virtual visit. Think of Amwell as 'build your own telehealth' and Teladoc as 'buy telehealth as a service.'

sections.heading: Hybrid Care Integration
sections.content: Amwell Converge excels at hybrid care - seamlessly blending virtual and in-person visits. Its TytoCare integration enables remote physical exams; Biobeat provides hospital-grade vital monitoring. Deep EHR embedding (Epic, Cerner) means virtual visits feel native to clinical workflows. Teladoc focuses on standalone virtual care with its own network, less integrated with existing health system operations.

sections.heading: Business Model Comparison
sections.content: Both are enterprise solutions without public pricing. Amwell Converge typically uses per-provider or per-visit licensing for health systems building their own programs. Teladoc uses PEPM (per-employee-per-month) for employer clients or per-visit for direct consumers. Amwell's cost depends on implementation complexity; Teladoc's cost depends on services purchased.

recommendations.when: You're a health system wanting to deliver virtual care with your own providers, deeply integrated with your EHR.
You're an employer or insurer wanting turnkey telehealth services without managing providers.
You need hybrid care - seamlessly blending virtual visits with in-person follow-ups in your facilities.
You want the largest virtual care network with 90M+ member scale and BetterHelp mental health integration.

faqs.q: What's the difference between Amwell and Teladoc's business models?
faqs.a: Amwell Converge is a platform - health systems use it to deliver virtual care with their own doctors. Teladoc is a service - it provides its own doctors to deliver virtual care. Amwell enables, Teladoc delivers.
Amwell has a consumer app, but Amwell Converge specifically is enterprise infrastructure for health systems. Consumers access Amwell through their health system or insurer, not typically directly.

Amwell Converge has deeper EHR integration by design - it's built to embed into Epic, Cerner, and other systems as if virtual care is native. Teladoc has standard integrations but operates more independently.
KLAS is a healthcare IT research firm. Amwell scores 80.1 and Teladoc scores 78.4 in virtual care categories. Both are well-regarded, with Amwell rated slightly higher for health system deployments.
